title: Taxation and Classification Schedules for Household Items
summary: This thread tracks the evolving lists (schedules) that categorize household items for duty-free or dutiable status. The lists have expanded to include modern appliances and construction-related items, reflecting changes in consumer goods and industrial project requirements.

evolution.classification: Transitioned from basic household appliances to a more complex list including construction materials and specific electronic equipment.
evolution.structure: Moved from simple lists to detailed schedules linked to specific legal definitions of baggage.

timeline.change: Established the initial schedule for dutiable and duty-free household items.
Updated the list of household appliances eligible for specific baggage treatment.
Expanded the scope of items categorized under household/office equipment schedules.

Passenger Baggage: This schedule provides a list of goods imported as baggage that are subject to specific customs duties and taxes. It specifically categorizes items that are not for personal or household use, baggage exceeding the allowed quantity of suitcases, and goods imported in commercial quantities.
Specific categories of household and personal items are liable for fixed duties and taxes when imported as baggage, regardless of the passenger's duty-free allowance.
Customs Duty: Fixed rates of customs duty and taxes are established for various household and electronic items imported as baggage, including televisions, home theatre systems, home appliances, and gold or silver bars.
The schedule outlines specific duty amounts based on item specifications such as the size of display panels, capacity of cooling appliances, or unit measurements for carpets and lighting fixtures.
Professional Auditor: Professional cameras and recording equipment are subject to a specified fixed amount of customs duty per unit when imported as baggage.

এস, আর, ও নং ১৫২-আইন/২০১৫/৩২/কাস্টমস।- Customs Act, 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969) এর section 219, উক্ত Act এর THIRD SCHEDULE এর item 17 এর সহিত পঠিতব্য, এ প্রদত্ত ক্ষমতাবলে জাতীয় রাজস্ব বোর্ড, ট্রান্সফার অফ রেসিডেন্স (Transfer of Residence) ব্যাগেজ (আমদানি) বিধিমালা, ২০০০ এর নিম্নরূপ অধিকতর সংশোধন করিল, যথা:-

উপরি-উক্ত বিধিমালার বিধি ৫ এ উল্লিখিত 'তালিকা' এর পরিবর্তে নিম্নবর্ণিত 'তালিকা' প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে, যথা :-

“তালিকা

টেলিভিশন সেট, রেফ্রিজারেটর, ডিপফ্রিজার, গৃহস্থালী কুকার ও ওভেন, ওয়াশিং মেশিন, ক্লথ ড্রায়ার, ডিসওয়াশার, ভি. সি. পি, ভি. সি. আর, সেলাই মেশিন, নিটিং মেশিন, মিউজিক সেন্টার, লেজার ডিস্ক প্লেয়ার/কম্প্যাক্ট ডিস্ক প্লেয়ার, ভিডিও প্লেয়ার, হোম থিয়েটার, সিডি/ডিভিডি, মুভি ক্যামেরা, ভিডিও প্রজেক্টর, সর্ব প্রকার ফ্যান, এয়ার কন্ডিশনার, এয়ারকুলার, টেলিফোন সেট (মোবাইলসেট সহ), ভিডিও ক্যাসেট (রেকর্ডকৃত), পারসোনাল কম্পিউটার/ল্যাপটপ, স্যাটেলাইট রিসিভার, ক্রোকারিজ বা তৈজসপত্র, আসবাবপত্র, নেবুলাইজার মেশিন, ক্রাচ (crutch), হুইল চেয়ার এবং অনধিক ১ (এক) হাজার মার্কিন ডলার মূল্যের অন্যান্য ব্যবহার্য গৃহস্থালী সামগ্রী।”

Customs Act 1969: Section 219 of the Act, when read in conjunction with item 17 of the Third Schedule, provides the legal basis for the National Board of Revenue to amend baggage rules.
National Board of Revenue: The board is empowered by the Customs Act to amend the Transfer of Residence Baggage (Import) Rules 2000.
Transfer of Residence Baggage (Import) R: The rules are amended to replace the existing list of household and personal items that are subject to the transfer of residence baggage provisions.
Third Schedule: Item 17 of this schedule is used in conjunction with the Customs Act to provide the authority for amending the current baggage rules.
Passenger Baggage Allowance: The list of permitted household and personal effects that qualify under the transfer of residence rules is updated to include specific electronic appliances, furniture, medical equipment, and other personal items up to a defined monetary threshold.

Consumable Goods: The schedule defines a list of items categorized as consumable goods for the purpose of the relevant legal clause. These items include construction materials, machinery parts, household items, and various industrial supplies that do not qualify for specific customs exemptions or treatment.
Steel Sheet: This category includes steel sheets defined by specific American Standard Testing Method specifications and thickness requirements.
Chemicals: All types of chemical products are classified under this schedule as consumable goods.
Household and Personal Baggage: Household goods are included within the list of consumable goods subject to the regulations specified in this notification.
Air Conditioner: Air conditioners with a cooling capacity up to a specified British Thermal Unit threshold are classified as consumable goods.
Imported Vehicle: Vehicles falling under specific headings of the First Schedule of the Customs Act 1969 are categorized as consumable goods for the purpose of this notification.
Customs Act 1969: The Act is referenced to define the classification headings for vehicles that are treated as consumable goods under this schedule.
First Schedule: The First Schedule of the Customs Act is used to identify specific vehicle classifications that are included in the list of consumable goods.
